invariants_assessed.INV-5: APPLIES. SATISFIED, verified against the real Letflow.Dlq code (not just design-doc assertion): get/2 does Repo.get(Entry, id, prefix: prefix); retry/2 and discard/2's shared fetch_and_lock_entry/3 does Entry |> where(id: ^id) |> lock("FOR UPDATE") |> repo.one(prefix: prefix) -- schema-per-tenant means a cross-tenant row is not merely filtered out by a predicate but physically unreachable from another schema's connection, so a genuinely-nonexistent id and a real-but-other-tenant id take the identical one-round-trip DB path and both resolve to {:error, :not_found}. Router-side: handle_get maps both {:error,:not_found} and {:error,:invalid_id} to the identical Response.not_found(conn) call (dlq.ex:161-166); handle_write_result does the same for retry/discard (dlq.ex:187-193). No distinguishing status/body. Timing: malformed-UUID short-circuits before any DB call, but that only distinguishes 'malformed input' from 'well-formed UUID', never 'cross-tenant real id' from 'genuinely absent id' (both of those take the identical query path) -- so INV-5's actual concern (cross-tenant vs never-existed indistinguishability) holds structurally, not just by status-code coincidence.
